title: Numeric-fidelity / reconciliation engine + citation-coverage ("no source, no figure")
context: Numeric fidelity is non-negotiable in Open-Spending-Explainers. A wrong figure in a budget explainer is actively harmful and erodes public trust. Every figure in an explainer must resolve to a citation pointing at a pinned source snapshot line item, and component figures must reconcile to stated totals within a disclosed rounding tolerance. Headline totals must match exactly. A non-reconciling or uncited figure must fail CI and cannot ship. Depends on ingest-006 (pipeline with checksummed snapshots).
objective: Implement the numeric-fidelity and reconciliation engine (lib/reconcile) that enforces two invariants: (1) citation coverage — every quantitative claim in an explainer must carry a resolving citation to a snapshot line item (no source, no figure); and (2) reconciliation — component figures sum to stated totals within a disclosed rounding tolerance, with headline totals matching exactly. Non-reconciling or uncited figures must fail CI.
acceptanceCriteria: Every figure in an explainer output must resolve to a citation pointing at a snapshot line item; a citation-coverage test enforces this with a build failure on any uncited figure
Component figures reconcile to stated totals within a disclosed rounding tolerance; headline totals must match exactly; a non-reconciling figure fails CI
Never conflates budgeted with actual; mismatches between basis fields surface as explicit CI failures rather than silent coercion
Reconciliation is run in CI as a release gate; any figure that does not reconcile or resolve cannot ship
DuckDB used for in-process tabular reconciliation and aggregation as specified in PLAN.md architecture
Tested on fixtures including reconciling cases, non-reconciling cases, and uncited-figure cases; PR merged with green CI and maintainer review passed
output: A merged PR containing the reconciliation and citation-coverage engine (lib/reconcile) that enforces citation coverage and numeric reconciliation as CI release gates, using DuckDB for in-process aggregation — the gate that ensures every shipped figure is sourced and reconciled.
